summary: An iOS and Android app sharing TypeScript schemas with its own API and Postgres database.
description: Build an Expo Router phone app and a Bun/Hono API together, sharing Zod schemas across the mobile screens and backend. Postgres and Drizzle are part of the base, with database-backed API tests and hooks that own client data access. The default Clerk fragment adds sign-in when configured. The first screen proves API connectivity; your screens, data model and authorization rules come next.
seoDescription: An Expo app for iOS and Android with a Hono API, shared TypeScript schemas and Postgres, plus Clerk sign-in in the default composition.

projectExamples.title: Personal reading log
projectExamples.description: Build book records and reading screens on the included API and Postgres. Configure default Clerk sign-in and enforce record ownership in your routes.

projectExamples.title: Field observation notebook
projectExamples.description: Add observation forms and API-backed records for iOS and Android. Photos, location access and offline synchronization need additional implementation and platform permissions.

requests: build one phone app for both major mobile platforms
keep my app screens and backend responses consistent through shared types
store my mobile app's data behind an API I control
give screens reusable hooks for loading data and handling failures
caveats: Entitlements such as Apple sign-in can require signing even for simulator builds; gate them to EAS builds.
